src/coordharness/coord/cli.py.origin: ported, then extended in this repository
src/coordharness/coord/cli.py.reason: Re-reviewed after adding standalone onboarding, generated client configuration, exact work-context reads, and typed fenced handoff commands; lifecycle writes remain explicit and database-scoped. Re-reviewed again after the CLI error-boundary pass: `--traceback` is declared for help text only, a claim collision is translated to a sentence naming the holder that the code reads back rather than infers, `work-context` now takes the not-found branch that `_work_row`'s empty-dict return had made unreachable, and `route` refuses a `--usage-db` path that is absent. No new write path and no change to any domain message. Re-reviewed after four client-surface additions: --write-scope on claim plus declare-write-set and conflicts, so the write-set overlap query the agent system prompt already instructs agents to use is reachable; owner session fields emitted beside the unchanged assignee; --to-session on note; and inbox binding to the reading session so a session-addressed note is visible from the shell. Existing output shapes gained fields and lost none. Re-reviewed after closing the claim-ownership hole: a claim_id was sufficient authority to mutate a claim held by another session, and the resulting row still attributed the action to the true holder. coord heartbeat-claim, release and done now pass this shell's resolved session identity to the coord_db mutators, so the CLI is covered by the same refusal as the MCP surface. No new command, no changed output shape. Re-reviewed after `coord create` stopped being an upsert: its existence check ran outside the write transaction and the write itself merged into whatever row it found, so two sessions choosing the same work id both reported "created": true and one silently overwrote the other. The verb now calls coord_db.create_work, which refuses a taken id from inside the transaction that inserts, and the emitted `created` is that call's measured result. No new command and no other changed output shape. Re-reviewed after `coord sign-off` and `coord release --reason` were added. sign-off is the only writer of operator_ok in the product and the one this file's `post_event` refusal has always named; it is deliberately absent from the MCP surface and gated on the invoking process's controlling terminal, read through /dev/tty rather than stdin, so a piped or scripted answer is never consulted. It resolves no lane identity and runs no lifecycle policy, because both read the ambient actor and an operator decision must not carry an agent's name. `release` gained `--reason`, the flag that reaches the `release_claim(reason=...)` parameter a blocked release has always required and this surface could not supply. No other command changed shape.

src/coordharness/coord/coord_db.py.origin: ported, then extended in this repository
src/coordharness/coord/coord_db.py.reason: import closure of the coordination control plane (coordharness.coord.coord_db). Re-reviewed after splitting the inbox into its directed and broadcast legs: `unread_inbox_counts` reports both plus their sum, `unread_inbox_count` now returns that sum so existing callers read the same figure, `read_inbox` labels every row `directed`, and its new `directed_only` argument is opt-in so the default reading returns the same SET of messages it always did. No new write path, no change to which events are recorded. Prior review of `post_note`, the `newest_first` option, and the session-close memory-proposal hook stands. Re-reviewed again after `claim_work` gained a pre-INSERT refusal for a work id that is not on the board: it replaces a foreign-key error with the id and where to look, cannot fire on the create-and-claim path that passes work_fields, and changes no other outcome. Re-reviewed again after `board_rows` began refusing a `group_by` that names no field on a work row: the old behaviour sorted every row into "(ungrouped)" and exited zero, so a typo and a real grouping were indistinguishable in the output. The refusal names the groupable fields. Read path only; no write path and no schema change. Re-reviewed after the session-granularity work: resolve_note_session_target validates a note's session target exists and is live and refuses a dead one; post_note accepts it with the lane default unchanged; board rows carry the owner session the v_work_owner view already computed. Also the successor pointer emitted at closeout now names a module a clone can run rather than a coordharness/scripts path no checkout contains. Re-reviewed after closing the claim-ownership hole: a claim_id was sufficient authority to mutate a claim held by another session, and the resulting row still attributed the action to the true holder. heartbeat_claim, release_claim and complete_claim now take the calling session's identity and refuse a caller that does not hold the claim, resolving the same session family the work_id path already resolves. CLAIM_MUTATION_SYSTEM_CALLERS is an enumerated door for the system paths (lease expiry, zombie reaping, typed handoff), each of which remains its own typed operation and passes nothing. No schema change. Re-reviewed after two coordination repairs. create_work is a new insert-or-refuse doorway for `coord create`, raising WorkIdCollisionError from inside the same transaction as its existence check; _upsert_work_unlocked gained an opt-in require_new flag and now returns whether it inserted, leaving the shared amend branch that fills fields on existing rows exactly as it was. apply_continuation_ready_transition now also accepts a requeue with no claim to release, for the blocked row whose claim lease expired and was released while the work item stayed sticky-blocked; it re-checks inside the transaction that no claim holds the row, so a row someone has taken is never requeued out from under them. No schema change. Re-reviewed after record_operator_sign_off was added: the typed human-only writer the public post_event refusal already named, and previously absent from the tree, leaving operator_ok schema, validators and consumers with nothing able to populate them. It mints the operator_ok event with actor=operator and trust=system and binds it to work_items.operator_ok_event_id under a compare-and-set in the same transaction, is replay-safe on an operation_id, and refuses a row with an open review barrier rather than recording a valid event that every reader then ignores. It writes no new column and changes no existing write path; post_event and upsert_work keep their refusals. The `operator-ok:` idempotency namespace is reserved in post_event alongside the two namespaces already reserved there, so a public writer cannot squat an operation id and turn a later real sign-off into a replay collision.

src/coordharness/jobs/launch.py.origin: ported, then extended in this repository
src/coordharness/jobs/launch.py.reason: The Claude-facing 'wrap any command so it appears on the board the instant it starts and is marked done/failed the instant it exits' launcher, with a hard RSS cap on the whole child tree (default 3 GB) so a runaway job gets killed long before the >6GB watchdog would ever notice. Pure-stdlib process supervision (Popen(start_new_session=True), ps -Ao pid=,ppid=,rss= summed over descendants every ~1s) — this is the most directly reusable, generic deliverable of the whole subsystem: 'coord jobs launch --job-id X --work-id Y --cap-gb 3 -- <command>'.

src/coordharness/jobs/sidecar_writer.py.origin: ported, then extended in this repository
src/coordharness/jobs/sidecar_writer.py.reason: The canonical job_progress sidecar WRITER: atomic tempfile+fsync+os.replace writes, monotonic pct/done within a run, terminal-state fencing so a late write can't resurrect or flip a finished job, appear()-on-start / update() / finalize()-refuses-premature-done, a wrapper-compatible write path for a shell launcher, and reconcile_dead() — a fail-closed repair that only reclassifies a stale RUNNING sidecar to failed after proving every recorded process identity is provably absent via kill(0). This is the write-side half of the sidecar contract docs/jobs-and-runs.md already documents (only the read-side — status.py/sidecar_snapshot.py/diagnostic_marker.py — was ported before). Its diagnostic_marker.py dependency (imported here as job_authority) already exists at the destination with matching function names (wrapper_control_lock, observe_control, publish_wrapper_control, new_launch_id, normalize_launch_id, canonical_sidecar_path, set/clear_diagnostic_marker), so the bulk of this file ports mechanically.
